feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: The economic squeeze is pushing up poverty rates for older adults
entry.summary: Despite lower poverty overall, the rate for seniors has been steadily rising in recent years. A new AARP survey sheds light on how those over 50 are struggling in the crucial time before retirement.

entry.title: FBI investigating after hackers say they took sensitive data from agency's jobs site
entry.summary: The FBI is investigating criminal hackers' claims of breaching its jobs website. The apparent hack poses a potential counterintelligence risk and a safety concern for employees and applicants.

entry.title: The Education Dept. hasn't been dismantled. It's become more inefficient, staff say
entry.summary: Education staff are being scattered across several other federal agencies. Despite the Trump administration's claims, employees say it's adding bureaucracy and making it harder to serve students.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: A judge has temporarily restored White House access for three media outlets barred by Trump, Trump and China's Xi Jinping will meet today, Israel's prime minister to speak at UNGA.

entry.title: Tucker Carlson on the war with Iran and why he worries about the spread of tribalism
entry.summary: For NPR's Newsmakers, Steve Inskeep asks Tucker Carlson about the war in Iran, President Trump and tribalism.

entry.title: Could the White House try its press ban again? A press freedom expert explains
entry.summary: A federal judge's ruling restored CNN, MS Now and Politico's access to the White House. Gabe Rottman says better procedure alone may not resolve the broader First Amendment fight.

entry.title: For their podcast, 2 elementary school students ask adults why they chose their jobs
entry.summary: Kids are used to being asked, "What do you want to be when you grow up?" Two students in Columbus, Ohio, flipped the script to ask grown-ups why they chose their careers.

entry.title: Journalists for CNN, MS NOW and Politico return to the White House upon judge's orders
entry.summary: A federal judge ordered the Trump administration on Thursday to temporarily restore access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico, after they were banned from covering White House events by President Trump.

entry.title: Judge considers restoring journalists' access to White House after Trump's ban
entry.summary: Lawyers representing the White House and the three media outlets banned from the property sparred over the constitutional rights of journalists at a hearing in federal court Wednesday.

entry.title: FBI records point to possible congressional pay-for-play scheme
entry.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Avi Asher-Schapiro of ProPublica about the connections between a defense contractor and Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, and how the FBI was, at one time, looking into it.
